current_bottleneck: 303a proves native recurrence can recover aggregate mean reversion, but the simple recurrent one-step transition flow loses joint cross-cell structure and daily-change/pathwise distributional realism. The pathology is now a dependence-factorization failure, not a support-validity or aggregate-MR failure.
last_result_summary: 303a-v0 scored 2/11, passing only block_ar and cointegration. It kept explosion 0.0% and achieved MR ratio 1.016 with h30 MR 0.920, but failed surface calendar validity, coverage calibration, conditionality, time-series tails, regime coverage, distributional fidelity, cross-cell correlation, and pathwise jumps. Cross-cell corr ratio collapsed to 0.297 with rank ratio 3.610, change KS was 3/25, level KS 0/25, and q99 jump cells 8/25.
next_step_recommendation: Run post-experiment analysis comparing 301a/302a/303a. Determine whether the recurrent factorization itself is too independent across cells, whether the one-step MLP velocity lacks a shared-factor noise geometry, or whether teacher-forced recurrent training is creating a free-run dependence gap. Do not add new components until that mechanism is quantified.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, 282b-v0, and 296c-v0 remain the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11.
current_best_note: 303a did not improve the frontier, but it isolated a useful tradeoff: recurrence solves aggregate MR while damaging cross-cell and pathwise law.
